name: Copper palmitoyl heptapeptide-14

lead: Copper palmitoyl heptapeptide-14 is a cosmetic peptide complexed with copper and attached to palmitic acid. It is used in anti-aging serums for firmer-looking skin.
It is a lesser-known relative of GHK-Cu, the popular copper peptide.

paras: Suppliers say copper peptides signal skin cells to support collagen and elastin, and the fatty-acid tail helps the molecule enter the skin surface.
Topical cosmetic use; irritation is the usual concern with any skincare product. No human trials of this specific ingredient were found.

studies.title: Activation of latent transforming growth factor beta 1 and inhibition of matrix metalloprotease activity by a thrombospondin-like tripeptide linked to elaidic acid.

chain: Applied in a serum or cream
angle.text: People add it through anti-aging serums aiming for firmer, smoother-looking skin. The palmitoyl group is intended to help the peptide sit in the skin's outer layers.

lead: Copper palmitoyl heptapeptide-14, also sold under the name Lipospondin in some listings, is a cosmetic ingredient made of a copper-bound, palmitic-acid-modified peptide. It is added to anti-aging serums and creams, where it is marketed for skin firmness and smoother-looking skin.

Suppliers describe it as a skin-conditioning copper peptide. It belongs to the wider family of copper peptides, the best known being GHK-Cu, which has been studied in small facial trials for firming and anti-wrinkle effects [1]. No published human trials of copper palmitoyl heptapeptide-14 itself were found.

paras: It appears in serums and creams aimed at fine lines and loss of firmness. Product pages from ingredient suppliers attribute collagen- and elastin-supporting activity to it.

The related tripeptide copper complex GHK-Cu, listed as Copper Tripeptide-1, is used in anti-aging and hair products, and small controlled facial studies reported firming and anti-wrinkle effects [1].
It is the copper salt of a heptapeptide joined to palmitic acid, a fatty acid that makes the molecule more oil-soluble. It is a cosmetic ingredient rather than a drug.
It is listed in the EU cosmetic ingredient inventory as a skin-conditioning agent. Copper peptides are common in skincare discussions among appearance-focused communities.
No studies found. Studies of the related copper peptide GHK-Cu in skin exist, but were small and short [1].
